title.zh: 卷56 列傳第21 盧愷 令狐熙 薛冑 宇文㢸 張衡 楊汪
title.en: Volume 56 Biographies 21: Lu Kai, Ling Huxi, Xue Zhou, Yu Wenbi, Zhang Heng, Yang Wang
title.raw: 卷56 列傳第21 盧愷 令狐熙 薛冑 宇文㢸 張衡 楊汪 Volume 56 Biographies 21: Lu Kai, Ling Huxi, Xue Zhou, Yu Wenbi, Zhang Heng, Yang Wang

sentences.zh: 隋書卷五十六列傳第二十一

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 56, Biography 21
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 56, Biography 21

sentences.zh: ○盧愷

translations.literal: ○ Lu Kai
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai

sentences.zh: 盧愷，字長仁，涿郡范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Kai, styled Changren, was a man of Fanyang in Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai, courtesy name Changren, came from Fanyang in Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父柔，終於魏中書監。

translations.literal: His father Rou ended his life as Director of the Secretariat of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rou had ended his career as director of the secretariat under Wei.

sentences.zh: 愷性孝友，神情爽悟，略涉書記，頗解屬文。

translations.literal: Kai's nature was filial and friendly; his spirit was clear and perceptive; he had slight involvement in writing and records, and was rather able at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was by nature filial and devoted to his brothers, quick-witted and sharp of mind. He had some familiarity with letters and records and was fairly skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲引為記室。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou summoned him as Master of Records.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi brought him in as master of records.

sentences.zh: 其後襲爵容城伯，邑千一百戶。

translations.literal: Thereafter he inherited the rank of Baron of Rongcheng, with a fief of 1,100 households.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the title Baron of Rongcheng, with a fief of eleven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從憲伐齊，愷說柏杜鎮下之。

translations.literal: Following Xian in the campaign against Qi, Kai persuaded Baidu Garrison to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Xian in the campaign against Qi, Kai talked the garrison at Baidu into surrendering.

sentences.zh: 遷小吏部大夫，增邑七百戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel, with his fief increased by 700 households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to senior clerk in the ministry of personnel and received seven hundred additional households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 染工上士王神歡者，嘗以賂自進，塚宰宇文護擢為計部下大夫。

translations.literal: A dye-work artisan senior officer Wang Shenhuan had once used bribes to advance himself; Grand Minister Yuwen Hu promoted him to Senior Clerk in the Accounting Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: A dye-work artisan named Wang Shenhuan had once bought his way forward; Grand Minister Yuwen Hu raised him to senior clerk in the accounting bureau.

sentences.zh: 愷諫曰：「古者登高能賦，可為大夫，求賢審官，理須詳慎。

translations.literal: Kai remonstrated, saying: "In antiquity, one who ascended high could compose poetry and qualify as a grandee; in seeking the worthy and examining officials, principle requires thorough care.
translations.idiomatic: Kai remonstrated: "In antiquity a man who climbed high and composed verse could qualify as a grandee. In seeking talent and assigning office, the principle demands careful deliberation.

sentences.zh: 今神歡出自染工，更無殊異，徒以家富自通，遂與搢紳並列，實恐惟鵜之刺，聞之外境。」

translations.literal: Now Shenhuan comes from dye work and has no other distinction; he has merely used family wealth to win access, and so stands alongside gentry officials—I truly fear the reproach of the lone pelican will be heard beyond our borders.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shenhuan rose from the dye pits without any distinction otherwise. He gained access solely through family wealth and now ranks beside the silk-gowned elite. I fear the sting of the proverb about a lone pelican among fine birds will be heard beyond our borders.

sentences.zh: 護竟寢其事。

translations.literal: Hu ultimately set the matter aside.
translations.idiomatic: Hu ultimately dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 建德中，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the Jiande era, his fief was increased by 200 households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiande reign, he received two hundred more households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉內史下大夫。

translations.literal: After a little over a year, he was transferred to Senior Clerk in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A year or so later he was transferred to senior clerk in the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝在雲陽宮，敕諸屯簡老牛，欲以享士。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was at Yunyang Palace and ordered the garrisons to select old oxen, intending to use them to feast the troops.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu was at Yunyang Palace, he ordered the garrisons to pick out old oxen, planning to use them to feed his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 愷進諫曰：「昔田子方贖老馬，君子以為美談。

translations.literal: Kai advanced in remonstrance, saying: "In the past Tian Zifang ransomed an old horse, and gentlemen took it as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: Kai stepped forward to remonstrate: "Long ago Tian Zifang ransomed an old horse—a deed gentlemen still praise.

sentences.zh: 向奉明敕，欲以老牛享士，有虧仁政。」

translations.literal: Just now in obeying the clear edict, you wish to use old oxen to feast the troops—this falls short of humane governance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the order just issued would slaughter old oxen to feed the troops. That falls short of humane rule.

sentences.zh: 帝美其言而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor applauded his advice and halted the plan.

sentences.zh: 轉禮部大夫，為聘陳使副。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Clerk in the Ministry of Rites and served as deputy envoy on the mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He was made senior clerk in the ministry of rites and served as deputy on the embassy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 先是，行人多從其國禮，及愷為使，一依本朝，陳人莫能屈。

translations.literal: Previously, envoys often followed Chen's ceremonial forms; when Kai became envoy, he followed his own court entirely, and the men of Chen could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, envoys had often followed Chen court etiquette. When Kai led the mission, he adhered entirely to Sui protocol, and the Chen side could not make him yield.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，李穆攻拔軹關、柏崖二鎮，命愷作露布，帝讀之大悅，曰：「盧愷文章大進，荀景倩故是令君之子。」

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year, Li Mu captured the two garrisons of Zhiguan and Baiya; Kai was ordered to compose a battle bulletin. The Emperor read it and was greatly pleased, saying: "Lu Kai's literary skill has greatly advanced—Xun Jingqian was indeed the son of a fine lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year, Li Mu took the garrisons at Zhiguan and Baiya. Kai was ordered to write the victory proclamation. The emperor read it with delight and said, "Lu Kai's writing has improved greatly. It is no wonder—Xun Jingqian was ever the son of a worthy father.

sentences.zh: 尋授襄州總管司錄，轉治中。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Registrar to the Governor-General of Xiangzhou and then transferred to Administering Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made registrar to the governor-general of Xiangzhou, then promoted to administering director.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，征拜東京吏部大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, he was summoned and appointed Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang he was summoned and appointed senior clerk of personnel in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，加上儀同三司，除尚書吏部侍郎，進爵為侯，仍攝尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was given the additional title Pillar of State, Third Rank, dismissed as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced in rank to Marquis, and still acted as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he received the additional title of pillar of state, third rank, was appointed vice minister of personnel, was raised to marquis, and continued to act as left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 每有敷奏，侃然正色，雖逢喜怒，不改其常。

translations.literal: Whenever he presented memorials, he was forthright and stern-faced; even when encountering joy or anger, he did not change his usual demeanor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he submitted memorials, he spoke plainly with a steady countenance. Neither favor nor wrath from the throne could shake his usual bearing.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉愷有吏幹，賜錢二十萬，並賚雜彩三百匹，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended Kai for his administrative capacity, granted him 200,000 coins, and bestowed 300 bolts of assorted silks, adding Attendant Cavalier at Large.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Kai's administrative talent, gave him two hundred thousand coins and three hundred bolts of mixed silks, and added the title attendant cavalier at large.

sentences.zh: 八年，上親考百僚，以愷為上。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Emperor personally examined the hundred officials and ranked Kai as superior.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor personally evaluated the bureaucracy and ranked Kai highest.

sentences.zh: 愷固讓，不敢受，高祖曰：「吏部勤幹，舊所聞悉。

translations.literal: Kai firmly declined and did not dare accept; Emperor Gaozu said: "Your diligence and capacity in the Ministry of Personnel are long known to me.
translations.idiomatic: Kai firmly declined, not daring to accept. Emperor Gaozu said, "Your diligence and competence in personnel matters are well known to me already.

sentences.zh: 今者上考，僉議攸同，當仁不讓，何愧之有！

translations.literal: Now that the superior rating is unanimous in opinion, when duty calls one should not yield—what is there to be ashamed of!
translations.idiomatic: Today you receive the top grade with unanimous agreement. When the honor is rightly yours, why refuse it out of false modesty!

sentences.zh: 皆在朕心，無勞飾讓。」

translations.literal: All of this is in my heart; there is no need for pretended modesty.
translations.idiomatic: It is all clear in my mind—spare yourself the show of deference.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜禮部尚書，攝吏部尚書事。

translations.literal: After a little over a year, he was appointed Minister of Rites and acted in the duties of Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A year or so later he was appointed minister of rites and also took charge of personnel affairs.

sentences.zh: 會國子博士何妥與右僕射蘇威不平，奏威陰事。

translations.literal: It happened that Academician He Tuo of the Imperial University was at odds with Vice Director Su Wei and memorialized Wei's hidden affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At this time He Tuo, a doctor of the imperial university, bore a grudge against Vice Director Su Wei and reported secret misconduct on Wei's part.

sentences.zh: 愷坐與相連，上以愷屬吏。

translations.literal: Kai was implicated by association and the Emperor handed Kai over to the legal authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was implicated in the case and the emperor turned him over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 憲司奏愷曰：「房恭懿者，尉遲迥之党，不當仕進。

translations.literal: The legal authorities memorialized against Kai: "Fang Gongyi was a follower of Yuwen Jiong and should not have been allowed to enter office.
translations.idiomatic: The prosecutors reported: "Fang Gongyi was a partisan of Yuwen Jiong and should never have been promoted.

sentences.zh: 威、愷二人曲相薦達，累轉為海州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei and Kai both bent the rules to recommend and advance him, repeatedly transferring him until he became Governor of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Kai repeatedly shielded and promoted him until he rose to governor of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 又吏部預選者甚多，愷不即授官，皆注色而遣。

translations.literal: Moreover, many candidates were pre-selected in the Ministry of Personnel; Kai did not immediately grant office but marked them in red and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, many candidates passed preliminary selection in personnel, but Kai would not appoint them immediately—he marked them in red and dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 威之從父弟徹、肅二人，並以鄉正征詣吏部。

translations.literal: Wei's cousins Che and Su were both summoned to the Ministry of Personnel as village magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's paternal cousins Che and Su were both summoned to personnel as village magistrates.

sentences.zh: 徹文狀後至而先任用，肅左足攣蹇，才用無算，愷以威故，授朝請郎。

translations.literal: Che's petition arrived late yet was appointed first; Su had a withered left foot and no talent to speak of, yet Kai, because of Wei, made him Gentleman for Court Appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Che's paperwork arrived late yet he was appointed ahead of others. Su had a crippled left foot and no discernible talent, yet Kai made him a gentleman for court appearance out of regard for Wei.

sentences.zh: 愷之朋黨，事甚明白。」

translations.literal: Kai's factional conduct was very clear.
translations.idiomatic: The evidence of Kai's clique-building was plain.

sentences.zh: 上大怒曰：「愷敢將天官以為私惠！」

translations.literal: The Emperor flew into a rage: "Kai dares to turn the offices of Heaven into private favors!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: "Kai dares to treat the court's offices as his personal patronage!

sentences.zh: 愷免冠頓首曰：「皇太子將以通事舍人蘇夔為舍人，夔即蘇威之子，臣以夔未當遷，固啟而止。

translations.literal: Kai removed his cap and knocked his head, saying: "The Crown Prince was about to appoint Transmission Officer Su Kui as palace attendant; Kui is Su Wei's son. I thought Kui was unfit for transfer and firmly memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Kai bared his head and prostrated himself: "The crown prince was about to appoint transmission officer Su Kui as palace attendant. Kui is Su Wei's son. I judged him unworthy of promotion and firmly petitioned to stop it.

sentences.zh: 臣若與威有私，豈當如此！」

translations.literal: If I had private relations with Wei, would I have acted thus!
translations.idiomatic: If I had private dealings with Wei, would I have done such a thing!

sentences.zh: 上曰：「蘇威之子，朝廷共知，卿乃固執，以徼身幸。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Su Wei's son is known to the whole court; you nevertheless held fast, seeking personal fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Everyone at court knows Su Wei's son. You held fast anyway—clearly seeking personal advantage.

sentences.zh: 至所不知者，便行朋附，奸臣之行也。」

translations.literal: As for those you did not know, you practiced factional attachment—that is the conduct of a treacherous minister.
translations.idiomatic: But for those you did not even know, you practiced favoritism. That is the conduct of a treacherous minister.

sentences.zh: 於是除名為百姓。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was stripped of rank and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒於家。

translations.literal: Before long he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he died at home.

sentences.zh: 自周氏以降，選無清濁，及愷攝吏部，與薛道衡、陸彥師等甄別士流，故涉黨固之譖，遂及於此。

translations.literal: From the Zhou dynasty onward selection had no distinction of pure and impure; when Kai acted in the Ministry of Personnel, he with Xue Daoheng, Lu Yanshi, and others discriminated among the gentry streams, and so he fell under the slanders of the faction of She Danggu.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhou times official selection had made no distinction between worthy and unworthy. When Kai took charge of personnel, he worked with Xue Daoheng and Lu Yanshi to sort the gentry by merit, and thus provoked the slander of She Danggu—which brought him to this end.

sentences.zh: 子義恭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yigong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yigong inherited his title.

sentences.zh: ○令狐熙

translations.literal: ○ Linghu Xi
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Xi

sentences.zh: 令狐熙，字長熙，燉煌人也，代為西州豪右。

translations.literal: Linghu Xi, styled Changxi, was a man of Dunhuang; for generations his family had been powerful magnates of the Western Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Xi, courtesy name Changxi, came from Dunhuang. His family had for generations been leading magnates of the western prefectures.

sentences.zh: 父整，仕周，官至大將軍、始、豐二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zheng served Zhou and reached the rank of Grand General and Governor of the two prefectures of Shi and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng served under Zhou, rising to grand general and governor of Shi and Feng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 熙性嚴重，有雅量，雖在私室，終日儼然。

translations.literal: Xi's nature was stern and weighty, with refined capacity; even in private quarters he remained dignified all day.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was stern and dignified, with a refined breadth of mind. Even in his own home he maintained a grave bearing from morning to night.

sentences.zh: 不妄通賓客，凡所交給，必一時名士。

translations.literal: He did not casually associate with guests; whoever he befriended was invariably a leading man of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He did not casually receive guests; every associate he made was a noted figure of the day.

sentences.zh: 博覽群書，尤明《三禮》，善騎射，頗知音律。

translations.literal: He broadly read the classics and was especially versed in 《Three Rites》; he was skilled at mounted archery and had considerable knowledge of music.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely among the classics and was especially learned in 《Three Rites》. He was skilled at mounted archery and had a fair knowledge of musical theory.

sentences.zh: 起家以通經為吏部上士，尋授都督、輔國將軍，轉夏官府都上士，俱有能名。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Senior Officer in the Ministry of Personnel through mastery of the classics, was soon appointed Commander and General Who Supports the State, and was transferred to Senior Officer of the Summer Office—all with reputations for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a senior officer in personnel through classical learning, then became commander and general who supports the state, and later senior officer of the summer office—winning a name for competence at each post.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother and nearly could not survive the grief.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother and nearly did not survive his grief.

sentences.zh: 其父戒之曰：「大孝在於安親，義不絕嗣。

translations.literal: His father admonished him, saying: "The greatest filial piety lies in bringing peace to one's parents; by right one must not cut off the line of succession.
translations.idiomatic: His father warned him: "The greatest filial piety is to bring your parents peace of mind. By duty you must not let the family line die out.

sentences.zh: 吾今見存，汝又只立，何得過爾毀頓，貽吾憂也！」

translations.literal: I am still alive, and you are my only son—how can you go so far in ruining yourself and leaving me in worry!
translations.idiomatic: I am still alive, and you are my only son. How can you destroy yourself like this and leave me in anguish!

sentences.zh: 熙自是稍加饘粥。

translations.literal: From then on Xi gradually took a little gruel.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Xi gradually began to take thin gruel.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除小駕部，複丁父憂，非杖不起，人有聞其哭聲，莫不為之下泣。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Junior Master of the Imperial Carriage; he again entered mourning for his father, and unless leaning on a staff he could not rise; whoever heard his weeping could not keep from weeping below him.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed junior master of the imperial carriage. He then mourned his father again, unable to rise without a staff. All who heard him weep wept in turn.

sentences.zh: 河陰之役，詔令墨縗從事，還授職方下大夫，襲爵彭陽縣公，邑二千一百戶。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Heyin, an edict ordered him to serve in ink-stained mourning garb; on return he was appointed Senior Clerk in the Bureau of Appointments, inherited the rank of Duke of Pengyang County, with a fief of 2,100 households.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Heyin an edict ordered him to serve while still in mourning garb. On his return he was appointed senior clerk in the bureau of appointments, inherited the title Duke of Pengyang, and received a fief of twenty-one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及武帝平齊，以留守功，增邑六百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Qi, for his merit as garrison commander his fief was increased by 600 households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu conquered Qi, his fief was increased by six hundred households for his service as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 進位儀同，曆司勳、吏部二曹中大夫，甚有當時之譽。

translations.literal: He advanced to Pillar of State, served successively as Senior Clerk in the Bureaus of Merits and Personnel, and had great reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to pillar of state and served in turn as senior clerk in the bureaus of merits and personnel, earning great renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪之際，熙以本官行納言事。

translations.literal: At the moment Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Xi acted in the duties of Chief Censor in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, Xi served in his existing post as acting chief censor.

sentences.zh: 尋除司徒左長史，加上儀同，進爵河南郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Chief Administrator of the Ministry of Education, given the additional title Pillar of State, and advanced to Duke of Henan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made left chief administrator of the ministry of education, given the additional title pillar of state, and raised to duke of Henan commandery.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾寇邊，以行軍長史從元帥元諧討之，以功進位上開府。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun raided the frontier, he went as Chief Administrator on campaign with Commander-in-Chief Yuan Xie to suppress them and, for merit, advanced to Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided the frontier, he served as chief administrator on campaign under Commander-in-Chief Yuan Xie. For his merit he was promoted to senior pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 會蜀王秀出鎮於蜀，綱紀之選，鹹屬正人，以熙為益州總管長史。

translations.literal: When Prince of Shu Xiu went out to govern Shu, the choice of administrators all fell on upright men, and Xi was made Chief Administrator to the Governor-General of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiu of Shu was sent to govern Shu, upright men were chosen to keep order, and Xi was appointed chief administrator to the governor-general of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 未之官，拜滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Before taking office he was appointed Governor of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take that post he was appointed governor of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時山東承齊之弊，戶口名簿籍類不以實。

translations.literal: At that time Shandong still suffered the abuses of Qi; household registers and name lists often did not reflect reality.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shandong still bore the abuses of Qi rule; household registers and name lists often did not reflect reality.

sentences.zh: 熙曉諭之，令自歸首，至者一萬戶。

translations.literal: Xi enlightened them and ordered self-surrender; those who came numbered 10,000 households.
translations.idiomatic: Xi explained the law to them and ordered voluntary surrender; ten thousand households came forward.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，風教大洽，稱為良二千石。

translations.literal: In several years of office, customs and instruction were greatly harmonized, and he was called a fine governor of two thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years in office customs and instruction were greatly improved, and he was hailed as an excellent governor.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年，上幸洛陽，熙來朝，吏民恐其遷易，悲泣於道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang the Emperor visited Luoyang; Xi came to court, and officials and people, fearing he would be transferred, wept along the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaihuang the emperor visited Luoyang. When Xi came to court, officials and commoners, fearing he would be transferred, wept along the road.

sentences.zh: 及熙複還，百姓出境迎謁，歡叫盈路。

translations.literal: When Xi returned again, the people went beyond the border to welcome and greet him, with shouts of joy filling the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi returned, the people went out beyond the border to welcome him, and cheers filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 在州獲白烏、白麞、嘉麥，甘露降於庭前柳樹。

translations.literal: In the prefecture white crows, white musk deer, and fine wheat appeared, and sweet dew fell on the willow tree before the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: While he governed, white crows, white musk deer, and fine wheat appeared in the prefecture, and sweet dew fell on the willow tree before his hall.

sentences.zh: 八年，徙為河北道行台度支尚書，吏民追思，相與立碑頌德。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director of Revenue of the Hebei Circuit Executive and the officials and people, cherishing his memory, together erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to director of revenue on the Hebei circuit executive. Officials and people, cherishing his memory, together erected a stele praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 及行台廢，授并州總管司馬。

translations.literal: When the executive was abolished, he was appointed Administering Director to the Governor-General of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit executive was abolished, he was appointed administering director to the governor-general of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後征為雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as Vice Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned as vice governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋為長史，遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Soon he became Chief Administrator, then was transferred to Grand Master for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became chief administrator, then was transferred to grand master for ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 後以本官兼吏部尚書，往判五曹尚書事，號為明幹，上甚任之。

translations.literal: Later, in his original post he additionally served as Minister of Personnel and went to decide the affairs of the five ministries, being called clear and capable; the Emperor greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while retaining his original post, he also served as minister of personnel and adjudicated the affairs of the five ministries. Known for clarity and competence, he enjoyed the emperor's great trust.

sentences.zh: 及上祠太山還，次汴州，惡其殷盛，多有奸俠，於是以熙為汴州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned from sacrificing at Mount Tai and stopped at Bianzhou, disliking its prosperity and the many scoundrels and ruffians, he therefore made Xi Governor of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from the sacrifice at Mount Tai and stopped at Bianzhou, he disliked the city's prosperity and its many scoundrels, and so appointed Xi governor of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 下車禁遊食，抑工商，民有向街開門者杜之，船客停于郭外星居者，勒為聚落，僑人逐令歸本，其有滯獄，並決遣之，令行禁止，稱為良政。

translations.literal: On taking office he forbade wandering food-vendors, suppressed merchants and artisans, blocked those who opened doors facing the street, compelled boat travelers who lodged outside the outer wall to settle in communities, ordered sojourners to return home, and decided and dispatched all delayed cases; orders were enforced and prohibitions observed, and it was called good governance.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he banned itinerant food-sellers, restrained merchants and artisans, shut doors that opened directly onto the street, forced boat travelers lodging outside the city wall into settled communities, ordered migrants to return home, and cleared all delayed cases. Orders were enforced and prohibitions obeyed, and his rule was praised as excellent.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，顧謂侍臣曰：「鄴都天下難理處也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and commended it, turning to his attendants and saying: "Ye City is the hardest place under Heaven to govern.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and praised it, telling his attendants, "Ye was the hardest place in the realm to govern.

sentences.zh: 敕相州刺史豆盧通，令習熙之法。

translations.literal: He ordered Governor of Xiangzhou Dou Lutong to study Xi's methods.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Dou Lutong, governor of Xiangzhou, to adopt Xi's methods.

sentences.zh: 其年來朝，考績為天下之最，賜帛三百匹，頒告天下。

translations.literal: That year he came to court; his performance review was the highest in the realm, and he was granted 300 bolts of silk and the announcement was issued throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That year he came to court. His performance review ranked first in the realm; he received three hundred bolts of silk, and the announcement was issued throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 上以嶺南夷、越數為反亂，征拜桂州總管十七州諸軍事，許以便宜從事，刺史以下官得承制補授。

translations.literal: Because the Yi and Yue of Lingnan repeatedly rebelled, he was summoned as Governor-General of Guizhou over seventeen prefectures with military authority, permitted to act as circumstances required; officials below governor could be appointed by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Yi and Yue peoples of Lingnan rebelled repeatedly, he was summoned as governor-general of Guizhou over seventeen prefectures with military authority, empowered to act as circumstances required. Officials below the rank of governor could be appointed on his authority.

sentences.zh: 給帳內五百人，賜帛五百匹，發傳送其家累，改封武康郡公。

translations.literal: He was given 500 men within the tent guard, granted 500 bolts of silk, provided relay transport for his household, and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Wukang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was given five hundred tent guards, five hundred bolts of silk, relay transport for his household, and was re-enfeoffed as duke of Wukang commandery.

sentences.zh: 熙至部，大弘恩信，其溪洞渠帥更相謂曰：「前時總管皆以兵威相脅，今者乃以手教相諭，我輩其可違乎？」

translations.literal: When Xi reached his post he greatly extended grace and trust; the chieftains of the stream valleys said to one another: "Former governors all coerced us with military might; now he instructs us with his own hand—how can we disobey?
translations.idiomatic: When Xi reached his post he greatly extended grace and trust. The chieftains of the stream valleys said to one another, "Former governors all coerced us with military might. Now he instructs us with his own hand—how can we disobey?

sentences.zh: 於是相率歸附。

translations.literal: Thereupon they submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 先是，州縣生梗，長吏多不得之官，寄政于總管府。

translations.literal: Previously the prefectures and counties were stubborn and ungovernable; chief officials often could not take office, and governance was entrusted to the governor-general's office.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the prefectures and counties had been stubborn and hard to govern; chief officials often could not take office, and administration was left to the governor-general's office.

sentences.zh: 熙悉遣之，為建城邑，開設學校，華夷感敬，稱為大化。

translations.literal: Xi sent them all out, built cities and towns, established schools, and both Chinese and barbarians were moved to respect him, calling it great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent them all to their posts, built cities and towns, and established schools. Both Chinese and indigenous peoples were moved to respect him, calling his rule a great transformation.

sentences.zh: 時有寧猛力者，與陳後主同日生，自言貌有貴相，在陳日，已據南海，平陳後，高祖因而撫之，即拜安州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time there was Ning Mengli, born on the same day as Chen's last ruler; he claimed his appearance had the signs of nobility. Under Chen he already held the South Sea; after Chen was pacified, Emperor Gaozu therefore comforted him and immediately appointed him Governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Ning Mengli, born on the same day as Chen's last ruler. He claimed his features marked him for nobility. Under Chen he had already held the South Sea. After Chen fell, Emperor Gaozu comforted him and immediately appointed him governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 然驕倨，恃其阻險，未嘗參謁。

translations.literal: Yet he was arrogant and insolent, relying on his rugged terrain, and never came to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was arrogant and insolent, relying on his rugged terrain, and never came to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 熙手書諭之 ，申以交友之分。

translations.literal: Xi wrote him a personal letter, explaining the bond of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wrote him a personal letter, appealing to the bond of friendship.

sentences.zh: 其母有疢，熙複遺以藥物。

translations.literal: His mother had an illness; Xi again sent her medicines.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, Xi once more sent her medicines.

sentences.zh: 猛力感之，詣府請謁，不敢為非。

translations.literal: Mengli was moved, came to the prefecture to request audience, and did not dare do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this, Mengli came to the prefecture to pay his respects and no longer dared misbehave.

sentences.zh: 熙以州縣多有同名者，於是奏改安州為欽州，黃州為峰州，利州為智州，德州為歡州，東寧為融州，上皆從之。

translations.literal: Because many prefectures and counties had the same names, he therefore memorialized to change Anzhou to Qinzhou, Huangzhou to Fengzhou, Lizhou to Zhizhou, Dezhou to Huanzhou, and Dongning to Rongzhou; the Emperor all approved.
translations.idiomatic: Because many prefectures and counties shared the same names, he memorialized to rename Anzhou as Qinzhou, Huangzhou as Fengzhou, Lizhou as Zhizhou, Dezhou as Huanzhou, and Dongning as Rongzhou. The emperor approved all the changes.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，上表曰：「臣忝寄嶺表，四載於茲，犬馬之年，六十有一。

translations.literal: After several years in office he memorialized: "I am entrusted to the region beyond the ridges; four years have passed. In the years of a dog's service I am sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he memorialized: "I am entrusted with the region beyond the ridges; four years have now passed. In the years allotted to a loyal servant I am sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 才輕任重，愧懼兼深，常願收拙避賢，稍免官謗。

translations.literal: My talent is slight and my burden heavy; shame and fear are both deep. I have long wished to withdraw my inadequacy and yield to the worthy, slightly escaping official slander.
translations.idiomatic: My talent is slight and my burden heavy; shame and fear weigh on me alike. I have long wished to withdraw my inadequacy and yield to the worthy, and so escape official blame.

sentences.zh: 然所管遐曠，綏撫尤難，雖未能頓革夷風，頗亦漸識皇化。

translations.literal: Yet the territory I govern is remote and vast, and pacification is especially difficult; though I have not been able suddenly to reform barbarian customs, I have gradually made them know imperial transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the territory I govern is remote and vast, and pacification is especially difficult. Though I have not been able to reform barbarian customs at a stroke, I have gradually made them recognize imperial civilization.

sentences.zh: 但臣夙患消渴，比更增甚，筋力精神，轉就衰邁。

translations.literal: But I have long suffered from wasting thirst, and recently it has grown worse; sinew, strength, and spirit progressively decline.
translations.idiomatic: But I have long suffered from wasting thirst, and lately it has grown worse. My sinews, strength, and spirit are failing by the day.

sentences.zh: 昔在壯齒，猶不如人，況今年疾俱侵，豈可猶當重寄！

translations.literal: Even in my prime I was still inferior to others; how much less now that illness attacks me together—how can I still bear a heavy trust!
translations.idiomatic: Even in my prime I was no match for others. Now that illness afflicts me as well, how can I still bear so heavy a charge!

sentences.zh: 請解所任。」

translations.literal: I request to be released from my post.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be released from my duties.

sentences.zh: 優詔不許，賜以醫藥。

translations.literal: A gracious edict did not permit it and granted him medicines.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict refused his request and granted him medicines.

sentences.zh: 熙奉詔，令交州渠帥李佛子入朝。

translations.literal: Xi received the edict and ordered the stream chieftain Li Fozi of Jiaozhou to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xi received the edict and ordered Li Fozi, a stream chieftain of Jiaozhou, to come to court.

sentences.zh: 佛子欲為亂，請至仲冬上道，熙意在羈縻，遂從之。

translations.literal: Fozi wished to rebel and requested to set out in mid-winter; Xi, intending to keep him on a loose rein, agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Fozi intended rebellion and asked to set out in mid-winter. Xi, intending to keep him on a loose rein, agreed.

sentences.zh: 有人詣闕訟熙受佛子賂而舍之，上聞而固疑之。

translations.literal: Someone went to the palace to accuse Xi of accepting bribes from Fozi and releasing him; the Emperor heard and firmly suspected.
translations.idiomatic: Someone went to the palace to accuse Xi of accepting bribes from Fozi and releasing him. The emperor heard and firmly suspected him.

sentences.zh: 既而佛子反問至，上大怒，以為信然，遣使者鎖熙詣闕。

translations.literal: Soon word came that Fozi had rebelled; the Emperor was greatly enraged, believing it true, and sent envoys to fetter Xi and bring him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Fozi had rebelled. The emperor was greatly enraged, believing the accusation true, and sent envoys to fetter Xi and bring him to court.

sentences.zh: 熙性素剛，鬱鬱不得志，行至永州，憂憤發病而卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Xi's nature had always been firm; depressed and unable to achieve his aims, on reaching Yongzhou he fell ill from grief and anger and died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had always been firm by nature. Depressed and unable to achieve his aims, he reached Yongzhou, fell ill from grief and anger, and died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 上怒不解，於是沒其家財。

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger did not subside, and so his family property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger did not subside, and his family property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 及行軍總管劉方擒佛子送于京師，言熙實無贓貨，上乃悟，於是召其四子，聽預仕焉。

translations.literal: When Campaign Commander Liu Fang captured Fozi and sent him to the capital, he said Xi truly had no bribe goods; the Emperor then understood, and summoned his four sons and permitted them to enter office.
translations.idiomatic: When campaign commander Liu Fang captured Fozi and sent him to the capital, he reported that Xi had truly taken no bribes. The emperor then understood and summoned his four sons, permitting them to enter office.

sentences.zh: 少子德棻，最知名。

translations.literal: The youngest son Defen was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son, Defen, was the most renowned.

sentences.zh: ○薛胄

translations.literal: ○ Xue Zhou
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhou

sentences.zh: 薛胄，字紹玄，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Zhou, styled Shao'xuan, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhou, courtesy name Shao'xuan, came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父端，周蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Duan was Governor of Cai Prefecture under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duan had been governor of Cai prefecture under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 胄少聰明，每覽異書，便曉其義。

translations.literal: Zhou from youth was clever; whenever he read unusual books he immediately understood their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was clever from youth. Whenever he read an unusual book he grasped its meaning at once.

sentences.zh: 常歎訓注者不會聖人深旨，輒以意辯之，諸儒莫不稱善。

translations.literal: He often sighed that commentators on the classics did not grasp the sages' deep intent and would argue by his own understanding; all the scholars praised his correctness.
translations.idiomatic: He often lamented that commentators on the classics missed the sages' deeper intent and would argue from his own understanding. The scholars all praised his insight.

sentences.zh: 性慷慨，志立功名。

translations.literal: His nature was generous; his ambition was to establish merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous by nature and aspired to establish merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 周明帝時，襲爵文城郡公。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou he inherited the rank of Duke of Wencheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming of Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Wencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 累遷上儀同，尋拜司金大夫，後加開府。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Pillar of State and soon appointed Senior Clerk in the Bureau of Metals, later added as Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to pillar of state, was soon appointed senior clerk in the bureau of metals, and later received the additional rank of pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，擢拜魯州刺史，未之官，檢校廬州總管事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was promoted and appointed Governor of Lu Prefecture; before taking office he inspected and managed the affairs of the Governor-General of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was promoted to governor of Lu prefecture. Before taking that post he was assigned to inspect the affairs of the governor-general of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋除兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor of Yan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及到官，系囚數百，胄剖斷旬日便了，囹圄空虛。

translations.literal: When he reached office there were several hundred bound prisoners; Zhou judged and decided them within ten days and the prisons were empty.
translations.idiomatic: When he took office there were several hundred prisoners in custody. Zhou judged and cleared them within ten days, and the prisons stood empty.

sentences.zh: 有陳州人向道力者，偽作高平郡守，將之官，胄遇諸途，察其有異，將留詰之。

translations.literal: There was a man of Chen Prefecture named Xiang Daoli who falsely posed as Governor of Gaoping Commandery and was going to take office; Zhou met him on the road, observed something strange about him, and was about to detain and question him.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Chen prefecture named Xiang Daoli had falsely posed as governor of Gaoping commandery and was on his way to take office. Zhou met him on the road, sensed something amiss, and was about to detain and question him.

sentences.zh: 司馬王君馥固諫，乃聽詣郡。

translations.literal: Assistant Governor Wang Junfu firmly remonstrated, and he therefore allowed him to proceed to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant governor Wang Junfu firmly remonstrated, and Zhou allowed him to proceed to the commandery.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，即遣主簿追禁道力。

translations.literal: He soon regretted it and immediately sent the chief clerk to pursue and detain Daoli.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted the decision and at once sent the chief clerk to pursue and detain Daoli.

sentences.zh: 有部人徐俱羅者，嘗任海陵郡守，先是已為道力偽代之。

translations.literal: There was a local man Xu Juluo who had once served as Governor of Hailing Commandery and had already been falsely replaced by Daoli.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Xu Juluo had once served as governor of Hailing commandery and had already been falsely replaced by Daoli.

sentences.zh: 比至秩滿，公私不悟。

translations.literal: By the time his term ended, neither public nor private parties had perceived it.
translations.idiomatic: By the time his term ended, neither officials nor the public had noticed the fraud.

sentences.zh: 俱羅遂語君馥曰：「向道力以經代俱羅為郡，使君豈容疑之？」

translations.literal: Juluo then said to Junfu: "Daoli has long replaced Juluo as governor by fraud—how can the governor tolerate suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: Juluo then said to Junfu, "Daoli has long replaced me as governor by fraud. How can you, sir, still harbor suspicion?

sentences.zh: 君馥以俱羅所陳，又固請胄。

translations.literal: Junfu, based on what Juluo stated, again firmly requested Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Junfu, relying on Juluo's account, again pressed Zhou firmly.

sentences.zh: 胄呵君馥曰：「吾已察知此人詐也。

translations.literal: Zhou rebuked Junfu, saying: "I have already observed that this man is a fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou rebuked Junfu: "I have already seen that this man is a fraud.

sentences.zh: 司馬容奸，當連其坐！」

translations.literal: The assistant governor harbors deceit—he should be implicated in the punishment!
translations.idiomatic: The assistant governor harbors deceit. He should share the punishment!

sentences.zh: 君馥乃止。

translations.literal: Junfu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Junfu then desisted.

sentences.zh: 遂往收之，道力懼而引偽。

translations.literal: He then went to arrest him; Daoli, in fear, confessed to the fraud.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to arrest Daoli, who in fear confessed to the fraud.

sentences.zh: 其發奸摘伏，皆此類也，時人謂為神明。

translations.literal: His uncovering of fraud and exposure of hidden wrongdoing were all of this kind; people of the time called him divine.
translations.idiomatic: His uncovering of fraud and exposure of hidden wrongdoing were all of this kind. People of the day called him uncannily perceptive.

sentences.zh: 先是，兗州城東沂、泗二水合而南流，氾濫大澤中，胄遂積石堰之，使決令西注，陂澤盡為良田。

translations.literal: Previously east of Yan Prefecture city the Yi and Si rivers joined and flowed south, flooding the great marsh; Zhou piled stones to dam them and made them break westward, and the marshes and pools all became good fields.
translations.idiomatic: Previously east of Yan prefecture city the Yi and Si rivers joined and flowed south, flooding a great marsh. Zhou piled stones to dam them and diverted the water westward, turning the marshes and pools into fertile fields.

sentences.zh: 又通轉運，利盡淮海，百姓賴之，號為薛公豐兗渠。

translations.literal: He also opened transport routes, with profit reaching the Huai and Hai; the people relied on it and called it the Xue Duke's Abundant Yan Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened transport routes, bringing profit to the Huai and Hai regions. The people relied on it and called it Duke Xue's Abundant Yan Canal.

sentences.zh: 胄以天下太平，登封告禪，帝王盛烈，遂遣博士登太山，觀古跡，撰《封禪圖》及儀上之。

translations.literal: Zhou, because the realm was at peace, considered the feng and shan rites the supreme glory of emperors, and therefore sent a doctor to ascend Mount Tai, observe ancient traces, and compose 《Diagram of the Feng and Shan》 and present the rites.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm at peace, Zhou regarded the feng and shan rites as the supreme glory of emperors. He sent a doctor to ascend Mount Tai, observe ancient traces, and compose a 《Diagram of the Feng and Shan》, then presented the rites.

sentences.zh: 高祖謙讓不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu modestly declined and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu declined out of modesty and would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 後轉郢州刺史，前後俱有惠政。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Governor of E Prefecture; before and after he had benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to governor of E prefecture, where his benevolent governance continued as before.

sentences.zh: 征拜衛尉卿，尋轉大理卿，持法寬平，名為稱職。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Grand Master for Imperial Entertainments, soon transferred to Grand Master for Law, held the law with breadth and fairness, and was called competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as grand master for imperial entertainments, soon transferred to grand master for law. He applied the law with breadth and fairness and was regarded as competent in office.

sentences.zh: 後遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射高熲稍被疏忌，及王世積之誅也，熲事與相連，上因此欲成熲罪。

translations.literal: At that time Left Vice Director Gao Jiong was gradually estranged and suspected; when Wang Shiji was executed, Jiong's affairs were connected, and the Emperor therefore wished to complete Jiong's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Left Vice Director Gao Jiong was gradually estranged and suspected. When Wang Shiji was executed, Jiong's affairs were implicated, and the emperor therefore wished to complete Jiong's guilt.

sentences.zh: 胄明雪之，正議其獄。

translations.literal: Zhou clearly cleared him and rightly judged his case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou plainly exonerated him and judged the case on its merits.

sentences.zh: 由是忤旨，械系之，久而得免。

translations.literal: Thereby he offended the imperial will, was shackled and imprisoned, and after a long time was released.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he offended the throne, was shackled and imprisoned, and only after a long while was set free.

sentences.zh: 檢校相州事，甚有能名。

translations.literal: He inspected and managed the affairs of Xiang Prefecture and had a great reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected and managed the affairs of Xiang prefecture and won a great reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 會漢王諒作亂并州，遣偽將綦良東略地，攻逼慈州。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled at Bingzhou, he sent the false general Qi Liang to advance east and attack, pressing Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Han rebelled at Bingzhou, he sent the false general Qi Liang to advance east and attack, pressing Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史上官政請援於胄，胄畏諒兵鋒，不敢拒，良又引兵攻胄，胄欲以計卻之，遣親人魯世范說良曰：「天下事未可知，胄為人臣，去就須得其所，何遽相攻也？」

translations.literal: Governor Shangguan Zheng requested aid from Zhou; Zhou feared Liang's military edge and did not dare refuse. Liang again led troops to attack Zhou; Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to say to Liang: "Affairs under Heaven are not yet knowable. Zhou as a minister must choose his stand according to what is fitting—why rush to attack each other?
translations.idiomatic: Governor Shangguan Zheng requested aid from Zhou. Zhou feared Liang's military edge and did not dare refuse. Liang then led troops to attack Zhou. Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to tell Liang, "Affairs under Heaven are not yet settled. Zhou, as a minister, must choose his stand according to what is fitting. Why rush to attack one another?

sentences.zh: 良於是釋去，進圖黎陽。

translations.literal: Liang thereupon released him and advanced to plan against Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang thereupon withdrew and advanced to plan against Liyang.

sentences.zh: 及良為史祥所攻，棄軍歸胄。

translations.literal: When Liang was attacked by Shi Xiang, he abandoned his army and returned to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xiang attacked Liang, Liang abandoned his army and fled back to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以胄懷貳心，鎖詣大理。

translations.literal: The court considered that Zhou harbored divided loyalty and fettered him to the Court of Law.
translations.idiomatic: The court considered that Zhou harbored divided loyalty and fettered him to the court of law.

sentences.zh: 相州吏人素懷其恩，詣闕理胄者百餘人，胄竟坐除名，配防嶺南，道病卒。

translations.literal: The officials and people of Xiang Prefecture had long cherished his grace; over a hundred went to the palace to plead for Zhou. Zhou ultimately was punished by removal from rank and assigned to guard Lingnan, dying of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people of Xiang prefecture had long cherished his kindness; more than a hundred went to the palace to plead for him. Zhou was ultimately stripped of rank and assigned to guard Lingnan, dying of illness on the road.

sentences.zh: 有子、獻，並知名。

translations.literal: He had sons named He and Xian, both renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons named He and Xian, both of whom became well known.

sentences.zh: ○宇文弼

translations.literal: ○ Yu Wenbi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenbi

sentences.zh: 宇文弼，字公輔，河南洛陽人也，其先與周同出。

translations.literal: Yu Wenbi, styled Gongfu, was a man of Luoyang in Henan; his ancestors came from the same source as Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenbi, courtesy name Gongfu, came from Luoyang in Henan. His ancestors shared a common origin with the house of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 祖直力覲，魏巨鹿太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhiliguan was Governor of Julu under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhiliguan had been governor of Julu under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父珍，周宕州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Governor of Dang Prefecture under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had been governor of Dang prefecture under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 弼慷慨有大節，博學多通，仕周為禮部上士。

translations.literal: Bi was generous and had great integrity, broadly learned and widely versed; he served Zhou as Senior Officer in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was generous and possessed of great integrity, broadly learned and widely versed. He served Zhou as senior officer in the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉使鄧至國及黑水、龍涸諸羌，前後降附三十餘部。

translations.literal: He once served as envoy to the state of Dengzhi and to the Qiang of Heishui and Longge; before and after, over thirty tribes submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as envoy to the state of Dengzhi and to the Qiang of Heishui and Longge. In all, more than thirty tribes submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 及還，奉詔修定《五禮》，書成奏之，賜公田十二頃，粟百石。

translations.literal: On return he received an edict to revise and fix 《Five Rites》; when the book was completed he presented it and was granted twelve qing of public fields and a hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he received an edict to revise and fix the 《Five Rites》. When the work was completed he presented it and was granted twelve qing of public fields and a hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 累遷少吏部，擢八人為縣令，皆有異績，時以為知人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Junior Clerk of Personnel, promoted eight men as county magistrates, all with unusual achievements; the age considered him a knower of men.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to junior clerk of personnel and promoted eight men to county magistrate, all of whom achieved unusual success. The age considered him a knower of men.

sentences.zh: 轉內史都上士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Officer of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to senior officer of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝將出兵河陽以伐齊，謀及臣下，弼進策曰：「齊氏建國，於今累葉，雖曰無道，籓屏之寄，尚有其人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was about to send troops to Heyang to attack Qi and consulted his ministers; Bi advanced a plan, saying: "The Qi state has established its realm through many generations; though it is said to be without the Way, in the charge of the frontier screen it still has its men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was about to send troops to Heyang to attack Qi and consulted his ministers. Bi advanced a plan: "The Qi state has stood for many generations. Though it is said to be without the Way, it still has men to hold its frontiers.

sentences.zh: 今之用兵，須擇其地。

translations.literal: In using troops now one must choose the place.
translations.idiomatic: In deploying troops now one must choose the ground carefully.

sentences.zh: 河陽衝要，精兵所聚，盡力攻圍，恐難得志。

translations.literal: Heyang is strategically vital and where elite troops gather; if one exhausts strength in siege, I fear it will be hard to achieve one's aim.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang is strategically vital and where elite troops gather. If one exhausts strength in siege, I fear it will be hard to achieve one's aim.

sentences.zh: 如臣所見，彼汾之曲，戍小山平，攻之易拔。

translations.literal: As I see it, at the bend of the Fen the garrison is on a small hill and level ground; attacking it is easy to capture.
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, at the bend of the Fen the garrison sits on a small hill on level ground. It can be taken with ease.

sentences.zh: 用武之地，莫過於此，願陛下詳之。」

translations.literal: Among places for employing troops there is none better than this; I wish Your Majesty to examine it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Among places for employing troops there is none better than this. I beg Your Majesty to consider it carefully.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，師竟無功。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not accept it, and the army ultimately had no success.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept it, and the campaign ultimately failed.

sentences.zh: 建德五年，大舉伐齊，卒用弼計。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiande he launched a great campaign against Qi and ultimately used Bi's plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiande he launched a great campaign against Qi and ultimately adopted Bi's plan.

sentences.zh: 弼於是募三輔豪俠少年數百人以為別隊，從帝攻拔晉州。

translations.literal: Bi thereupon recruited several hundred bold young men of the Three Adjuncts as a separate detachment and followed the Emperor in capturing Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bi thereupon recruited several hundred bold young men of the three adjuncts as a separate detachment and followed the emperor in capturing Jin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 身被三創，苦戰不息，帝奇而壯之。

translations.literal: His body received three wounds; he fought bitterly without ceasing; the Emperor marveled and considered him strong.
translations.idiomatic: His body received three wounds, yet he fought on without ceasing. The emperor marveled and considered him strong.

sentences.zh: 後從帝平齊，以功拜上儀同，封武威縣公，邑千五百戶，賜物千五百段，奴婢百五十口，馬牛羊千餘頭，拜司州總管司錄。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Emperor in pacifying Qi; for merit he was appointed Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei County with a fief of 1,500 households, granted 1,500 bolts of goods, 150 slaves and maidservants, and over a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and appointed Registrar to the Governor-General of Si Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed the emperor in pacifying Qi. For his merit he was appointed pillar of state, enfeoffed as duke of Wuwei county with a fief of fifteen hundred households, granted fifteen hundred bolts of goods, a hundred fifty slaves and maidservants, and more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and was made registrar to the governor-general of Si prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，遷左守廟大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was transferred to Left Guardian of the Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was transferred to left guardian of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 時突厥寇甘州，帝令侯莫陳昶率兵擊之，弼為監軍。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks raided Gan Prefecture; the Emperor ordered Hou Mo Chen Chang to lead troops to attack them, with Bi as supervising general.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Turks raided Gan prefecture. The emperor ordered Hou Mo Chen Chang to lead troops against them, with Bi as supervising general.

sentences.zh: 謂昶曰：「黠虜之勢，來如激矢，去若絕弦，若欲追躡，良為難及。

translations.literal: He said to Chang: "The force of cunning barbarians comes like a rushing arrow and departs like a broken bowstring; if one wishes to pursue and overtake them, it is truly hard to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: He told Chang, "The force of cunning barbarians comes like a rushing arrow and departs like a broken bowstring. To pursue and overtake them is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 且宜選精騎，直趨祁連之西。

translations.literal: For the moment one should select elite cavalry and strike straight west of Qilian.
translations.idiomatic: For the moment one should choose elite cavalry and strike directly west of Qilian.

sentences.zh: 賊若收軍，必自蓼泉之北，此地險隘，兼複下濕，度其人馬，三日方度，緩轡追討，何慮不及？

translations.literal: If the bandits withdraw their army, they will necessarily come from north of Liaoyuan; that place is narrow and dangerous and also low and wet; estimating their men and horses, three days are needed to cross. With loose reins pursue and attack—why worry about not catching up?
translations.idiomatic: If the bandits withdraw, they will necessarily come from north of Liaoyuan. That place is narrow and dangerous and also low and wet. Estimating their men and horses, three days are needed to cross. With loose reins pursue and attack—why worry about not catching up?

sentences.zh: 彼勞我逸，破之必矣。

translations.literal: They will be weary while we are rested; breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: They will be weary while we are rested. Breaking them is certain.

sentences.zh: 若邀此路，真上策也。」

translations.literal: If one intercepts this route, it is truly the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: If one blocks this route, it is truly the superior strategy.

sentences.zh: 昶不能用之，西取合黎，大軍行遲，虜已出塞。

translations.literal: Chang could not use it and went west to take Heli; the great army moved slowly and the barbarians had already left the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Chang could not adopt it and went west to take Heli. The main army moved slowly and the barbarians had already left the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其年，弼又率兵從梁士彥攻拔壽陽，尋改封安樂縣公，增邑六百戶，賜物六百段，加以口馬。

translations.literal: That year Bi again led troops with Liang Shiyan to capture Shouyang; soon he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Anle County, with his fief increased by 600 households and 600 bolts of goods granted, with mouths and horses added.
translations.idiomatic: That year Bi again led troops with Liang Shiyan to capture Shouyang. Soon he was re-enfeoffed as duke of Anle county, with his fief increased by six hundred households and six hundred bolts of goods granted, with dependents and horses added.

sentences.zh: 除澮州刺史，俄轉南司州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Huai Prefecture and soon transferred to Governor of South Si Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Huai prefecture and soon transferred to governor of South Si prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後司馬消難之奔陳也，弼追之不及。

translations.literal: Later when Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, Bi pursued but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, Bi gave chase but failed to overtake him.

sentences.zh: 遇陳將樊毅，戰於漳口，自旦及午，三戰三捷，虜獲三千人。

translations.literal: He encountered Chen General Fan Yi and fought at the mouth of the Zhang River from dawn till noon; three battles, three victories; captives and booty numbered 3,000 men.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered Chen general Fan Yi and fought at the mouth of the Zhang River from dawn till noon. Three battles brought three victories, with three thousand captives and booty.

sentences.zh: 除黃州刺史，尋轉南定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Huang Prefecture and soon transferred to Governor of South Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Huang prefecture and soon transferred to governor of South Ding prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以前功封平昌縣公，加邑一千二百戶，入為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, for previous merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingchang County with his fief increased by 1,200 households and entered office as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang, for previous merit he was enfeoffed as duke of Pingchang county with his fief increased by twelve hundred households and entered office as right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時西羌內附，詔弼持節安集之，置鹽澤、蒲昌二郡而還。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Qiang submitted internally; an edict ordered Bi to hold credentials and pacify them, establishing the two commanderies of Yanzhe and Puchang, then returning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the western Qiang submitted internally. An edict ordered Bi to hold credentials and pacify them. He established the two commanderies of Yanzhe and Puchang, then returned.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，當官正色，為百僚所憚，三年，突厥寇甘州，以行軍司馬從元帥竇榮定擊破之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; in office he was stern-faced, and the hundred officials feared him. In the third year the Turks raided Gan Prefecture; as Campaign Administering Director he followed Commander-in-Chief Dou Rongding and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left vice director of the secretariat. In office he was stern-faced, and the hundred officials feared him. In the third year the Turks raided Gan prefecture. As campaign administering director he followed commander-in-chief Dou Rongding and broke them.

sentences.zh: 還除太僕少卿，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed vice minister of the imperial stud and transferred to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，楊素出信州道，令弼持節為諸軍節度，仍領行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, Yang Su went by the Xin Prefecture route; he ordered Bi to hold credentials as coordinator of the armies and still lead as Campaign Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign to pacify Chen, Yang Su went by the Xin prefecture route. He ordered Bi to hold credentials as coordinator of the armies and still lead as campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恩之破陳將呂仲肅也，弼有謀焉。

translations.literal: When Liu Ren'en defeated Chen General Lü Zhongsu, Bi had a share in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ren'en defeated Chen general Lü Zhongsu, Bi had a share in the planning.

sentences.zh: 加開府，擢拜刑部尚書，領太子虞候率。

translations.literal: He was given the additional rank Pillar of State, promoted and appointed Minister of Punishments, and led the Crown Prince's Guard of Honored Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He received the additional rank pillar of state, was promoted to minister of punishments, and led the crown prince's guard of honored attendants.

sentences.zh: 上嘗親臨釋奠，弼與博士論議，詞致清遠，觀者屬目。

translations.literal: The Emperor once personally attended the libation sacrifice; Bi debated with the doctors, his words clear and far-reaching, and observers fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once personally attended the libation sacrifice. Bi debated with the doctors, his words clear and far-reaching, and observers fixed their eyes on him.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，顧謂侍臣曰：「朕今睹周公之制禮，見宣尼之論孝，實慰朕心。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and, turning to his attendants, said: "Today I behold the Duke of Zhou's establishment of rites and see Confucius's discussion of filial piety—it truly comforts my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and, turning to his attendants, said, "Today I behold the Duke of Zhou's establishment of rites and see Confucius's discussion of filial piety. It truly comforts my heart.

sentences.zh: 於是頒賜各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon rewards were distributed to each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were then distributed to each according to rank.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷以晉陽為重鎮，并州總管必屬親王，其長史、司馬亦一時高選。

translations.literal: At that time the court considered Jinyang a heavy garrison; the Governor-General of Bingzhou necessarily belonged to an imperial prince, and the Chief Administrator and Administering Director were also chosen from the finest men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court considered Jinyang a heavy garrison. The governor-general of Bingzhou necessarily belonged to an imperial prince, and the chief administrator and administering director were also chosen from the finest men of the age.

sentences.zh: 前長史王韶卒，以弼有文武幹用，出為并州長史。

translations.literal: The former Chief Administrator Wang Shao died; because Bi had civil and military capacity he was sent out as Chief Administrator of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The former chief administrator Wang Shao died. Because Bi had civil and military capacity he was sent out as chief administrator of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄以父艱去職，尋詔起之。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on account of mourning for his father; soon an edict recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office to mourn his father. An edict soon recalled him to service.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遼東之役，授元帥漢王府司馬，仍尋領行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, in the Liaodong campaign, he was appointed Administering Director to the Prince of Han's headquarters and soon also led as Campaign Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, in the Liaodong campaign, he was appointed administering director to the prince of Han's headquarters and soon also led as campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 軍還之後，曆朔、代、吳三州總管，皆有能 名。

translations.literal: After the army returned he successively served as Governor-General of the three prefectures of Shuo, Dai, and Wu, all with reputations for competence.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he successively served as governor-general of Shuo, Dai, and Wu prefectures, winning a name for competence at each post.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，征拜刑部尚書，仍持節巡省河北。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was summoned as Minister of Punishments and still held credentials to inspect Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was summoned as minister of punishments and still held credentials to inspect Hebei.

sentences.zh: 還除泉州刺史。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Governor of Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed governor of Quan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，複拜刑部尚書，尋轉禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After a little over a year he was again appointed Minister of Punishments and soon transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A year or so later he was again appointed minister of punishments and soon transferred to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 弼既以才能著稱，曆職顯要，聲望甚重，物議時談，多見推許，帝頗忌之。

translations.literal: Bi, because his talent and capacity were renowned, held successive prominent posts, and his reputation was very weighty; public discussion at the time often praised him, and the Emperor was rather jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's talent and capacity were renowned, and he held successive prominent posts. His reputation was very weighty, and public discussion often praised him. The emperor grew jealous.

sentences.zh: 時帝漸好聲色，尤勤遠略，弼謂高熲曰：「昔周天元好聲色而國亡，以今方之，不亦甚乎？」

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns; Bi said to Gao Jiong: "In the past Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou favored music and women and the state perished—compared with today, is it not even more so?
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns. Bi said to Gao Jiong, "In the past Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou favored music and women and the state perished. Compared with today, is it not even worse?

sentences.zh: 又言：「長城之役，幸非急務。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The Great Wall labor service is fortunately not an urgent task."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The Great Wall labor service is fortunately not an urgent task."

sentences.zh: 有人奏之，竟坐誅死，時年六十二，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Someone memorialized this; he ultimately was punished by execution and died, aged sixty-two; all under Heaven considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported this. He was ultimately executed at sixty-two, and all under Heaven considered it unjust.

sentences.zh: 所著辭賦二十餘萬言，為《尚書》、《孝經注》行于時。

translations.literal: His writings in prose and fu numbered over 200,000 words; he made 《Notes on the Documents》 and 《Notes on the Classic of Filial Piety》 that circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His writings in prose and fu numbered over two hundred thousand words. He produced 《Notes on the Documents》 and 《Notes on the Classic of Filial Piety》 that circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 有子儉、瑗。

translations.literal: He had sons named Jian and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Jian and Yuan.

sentences.zh: ○張衡

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Heng
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng

sentences.zh: 張衡，字建平，河內人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng, styled Jianping, was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng, courtesy name Jianping, came from Henei.

sentences.zh: 祖嶷，魏河陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ni was Governor of Heyang under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ni had been governor of Heyang under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父光，周萬州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Guang was Governor of Wan Prefecture under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang had been governor of Wan prefecture under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 衡幼懷志尚，有骨鯁之風。

translations.literal: From youth Heng cherished ambition and integrity and had the air of unyielding bone.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Heng cherished ambition and integrity and had an unyielding spirit.

sentences.zh: 年十五，詣太學受業，研精覃思，為同輩所推。

translations.literal: At fifteen he went to the Imperial Academy to receive instruction, refining his study with deep thought, and was pushed forward by his peers.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he went to the imperial academy to study, refining his learning with deep thought, and was esteemed by his peers.

sentences.zh: 周武帝居太后憂，與左右出獵，衡露發輿櫬，扣馬切諫。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for the Empress Dowager and went hunting with those at his side; Heng bared his head and coffin-cloth, seized the horse, and remonstrated urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for the empress dowager and went hunting with those at his side. Heng bared his head and wore mourning cloth, seized the horse, and remonstrated urgently.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉焉，賜衣一襲，馬一匹，擢拜漢王侍讀。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended him, granted one suit of clothes and one horse, and promoted him as Reader to the Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him, granted one suit of clothes and one horse, and promoted him as reader to the prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 衡又就沈重受《三禮》，略究大旨。

translations.literal: Heng again studied 《Three Rites》 under Shen Chong and broadly grasped their great intent.
translations.idiomatic: Heng also studied the 《Three Rites》 under Shen Chong and came to grasp their larger meaning.

sentences.zh: 累遷掌朝大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Grand Master for the Court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand master for the court.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜司門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was appointed vice minister of the gate office.

sentences.zh: 及晉王廣為河北行台，衡曆刑部、度支二曹郎。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang became Hebei Executive, Heng served successively as Senior Clerk in the Bureaus of Punishments and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guang of Jin became Hebei executive, Heng served successively as senior clerk in the bureaus of punishments and revenue.

sentences.zh: 後以台廢，拜并州總管掾。

translations.literal: Later, when the executive was abolished, he was appointed Aide to the Governor-General of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the executive was abolished, he was appointed aide to the governor-general of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及王轉牧揚州，衡複為掾，王甚親任之。

translations.literal: When the Prince transferred to govern Yangzhou, Heng again became his aide; the Prince greatly trusted and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince transferred to govern Yangzhou, Heng again became his aide. The prince greatly trusted and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 衡亦竭慮盡誠事之，奪宗之計，多衡所建也。

translations.literal: Heng also exhausted his mind and gave full loyalty in serving him; the plan to seize the succession was largely Heng's creation.
translations.idiomatic: Heng also exhausted his mind and gave full loyalty in serving him. The plan to seize the succession was largely Heng's creation.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，歲餘，起授揚州總管司馬，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother; after a little over a year he was recalled and appointed Administering Director to the Governor-General of Yangzhou, granted 300 bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother. A year or so later he was recalled and appointed administering director to the governor-general of Yangzhou, granted three hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，熙州李英林聚眾反，署置百官，以衡為行軍總管，率步騎五萬人討平之。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang, Li Yinglin of Xizhou gathered a crowd and rebelled, appointing officials; Heng was made Campaign Commander and led 50,000 infantry and cavalry to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang, Li Yinglin of Xizhou gathered a crowd and rebelled, appointing officials. Heng was made campaign commander and led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 拜開府，賜奴婢一百三十口，物五百段，金銀雜畜稱是。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pillar of State, granted 130 slaves and maidservants, 500 bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed pillar of state, granted a hundred thirty slaves and maidservants, five hundred bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.

sentences.zh: 及王為皇太子，拜衡右庶子，仍領給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Prince became Crown Prince, Heng was appointed Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and still led as Supervising Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Heng was appointed right assistant to the heir apparent and still served as supervising attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，除給事黃門侍郎，進位銀青光祿大夫，俄遷御史大夫，甚見親重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was appointed Supervising Attendant of the Yellow Gate, advanced to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace, and soon transferred to Censor-in-Chief; he was greatly trusted and honored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was appointed supervising attendant of the yellow gate, advanced to silver-gleaming grand master of the palace, and soon transferred to censor-in-chief. He was greatly trusted and honored.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，帝幸榆林郡，還至太原，謂衡曰：「朕欲過公宅，可為朕作主人。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye the Emperor visited Yulin Commandery; on returning to Taiyuan he said to Heng: "I wish to pass your residence—you can act as host for me.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye the emperor visited Yulin commandery. On returning to Taiyuan he said to Heng, "I wish to pass your residence. You can act as host for me.

sentences.zh: 衡於是馳至河內，與宗族具牛酒。

translations.literal: Heng thereupon galloped to Henei and with his clan prepared oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Heng thereupon raced to Henei, where he and his clan prepared oxen and wine.

sentences.zh: 帝上太行，開直道九十裡，以抵其宅。

translations.literal: The Emperor ascended the Taihang Mountains and opened a straight road ninety li to reach his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the Taihang Mountains and opened a straight road ninety li to reach his residence.

sentences.zh: 帝悅其山泉，留宴三日，因謂衡曰：「往從先皇拜太山之始，途經洛陽，瞻望於此，深恨不得相過，不謂今日得諧宿願。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased with its mountain springs and remained feasting three days; he therefore said to Heng: "When I followed the late Emperor in beginning the sacrifice at Mount Tai and passed by Luoyang, I looked toward this place and deeply regretted that I could not visit— I did not expect today to fulfill my long-held wish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with its mountain springs and remained feasting three days. He then said to Heng, "When I followed the late emperor in beginning the sacrifice at Mount Tai and passed by Luoyang, I looked toward this place and deeply regretted that I could not visit. I did not expect today to fulfill my long-held wish.

sentences.zh: 衡俯伏辭謝，奉斛上壽。

translations.literal: Heng prostrated himself in apology and presented a hu of wine to wish long life.
translations.idiomatic: Heng prostrated himself in thanks and offered a hu of wine to wish the emperor long life.

sentences.zh: 帝益歡，賜其宅傍田三十頃，良馬一匹，金帶，縑彩六百段，衣一襲，禦食器一具。

translations.literal: The Emperor was even more pleased and granted thirty qing of good fields beside his residence, one fine horse, a gold belt, 600 bolts of silk, one suit of clothes, and one set of imperial dining vessels.
