translations.idiomatic: The emperor was even more pleased and granted thirty qing of good fields beside his residence, one fine horse, a gold belt, six hundred bolts of silk, one suit of clothes, and one set of imperial dining vessels.

sentences.zh: 衡固讓，帝曰：「天子所至稱幸者，蓋為此也，不足為辭。」

translations.literal: Heng firmly declined; the Emperor said: "Where the Son of Heaven arrives and calls it an imperial visit, it is for this; it is not enough to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Heng firmly declined. The emperor said, "Where the Son of Heaven arrives and calls it an imperial visit, it is for this. There is no need to decline.

sentences.zh: 衡複獻食於帝，帝令頒賜公卿，下至衛士，無不沾洽。

translations.literal: Heng again presented food to the Emperor; the Emperor ordered it distributed to the dukes and ministers down to the guards—none went without share.
translations.idiomatic: Heng again presented food to the emperor. The emperor ordered it distributed to the dukes and ministers down to the guards—none went without share.

sentences.zh: 衡以籓邸之舊，恩寵莫與為比，頗自驕貴。

translations.literal: Heng, because of his old ties in the princely residence, enjoyed favor unmatched by any; he became rather proud and self-important.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his old ties in the princely residence, Heng enjoyed favor unmatched by any and became rather proud and self-important.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝幸汾陽宮，宴從官，特賜絹五百匹。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor visited Fenyang Palace and feasted the accompanying officials, specially granting 500 bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor visited Fenyang Palace and feasted the accompanying officials, specially granting five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲大汾陽宮，令衡與紀弘整具圖奏之。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor wished to enlarge Fenyang Palace and ordered Heng and Ji Hongzheng to prepare diagrams and present them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor wished to enlarge Fenyang Palace and ordered Heng and Ji Hongzheng to prepare diagrams and present them.

sentences.zh: 衡承間進諫曰：「比年勞役繁多，百姓疲敝，伏願留神，稍加折損。」

translations.literal: Heng seized an opportunity to advance in remonstrance, saying: "In recent years corvée labor has been numerous and the people weary and exhausted; I humbly wish Your Majesty to keep this in mind and slightly reduce and cut back.
translations.idiomatic: Heng seized an opportunity to remonstrate: "In recent years corvée labor has been numerous and the people weary and exhausted. I humbly beg Your Majesty to keep this in mind and slightly reduce the burden.

sentences.zh: 帝意甚不平。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 後嘗目衡謂侍臣曰：「張衡自謂由其計畫，令我有天下也。」

translations.literal: Later he once looked at Heng and said to his attendants: "Zhang Heng considers that through his planning he gave me the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Later he once looked at Heng and said to his attendants, "Zhang Heng considers that through his planning he gave me the realm under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 時齊王暕失愛於上，帝密令人求暕罪失。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qi Yan had lost the Emperor's favor; the Emperor secretly ordered men to seek Yan's faults.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Yan of Qi had lost the emperor's favor. The emperor secretly ordered men to seek Yan's faults.

sentences.zh: 有人譖暕違制，將伊闕令皇甫詡從之汾陽宮。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Yan for violating regulations, having Yique Magistrate Huangfu Xu follow him to Fenyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Yan for violating regulations, having Yique magistrate Huangfu Xu follow him to Fenyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 又錄前幸涿郡及祠恆岳時，父老謁見者衣冠多不整。

translations.literal: He also recorded that when the Emperor previously visited Zhuo Commandery and sacrificed at Mount Heng, many of the elders who came to audience were not properly dressed.
translations.idiomatic: He also recorded that when the emperor previously visited Zhuo commandery and sacrificed at Mount Heng, many of the elders who came to audience were not properly dressed.

sentences.zh: 帝譴衡以憲司皆不能舉正，出為榆林太守。

translations.literal: The Emperor blamed Heng because the censorate all could not investigate and correct this, and sent him out as Governor of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Heng because the censorate could not investigate and correct this, and sent him out as governor of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝複幸汾陽宮，衡督役築樓煩城，因而謁帝。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor again visited Fenyang Palace; Heng supervised labor building Loufan city and thereby had audience with the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor again visited Fenyang Palace. Heng supervised labor building Loufan city and thereby had audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝惡衡不損瘦，以為不念咎，因謂衡曰：「公甚肥澤，宜且還郡。」

translations.literal: The Emperor disliked that Heng had not grown thin and considered that he did not reflect on his fault; he therefore said to Heng: "You are very plump and sleek—you should for the moment return to your commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor disliked that Heng had not grown thin and considered that he did not reflect on his fault. He therefore said to Heng, "You are very plump and sleek. You should for the moment return to your commandery.

sentences.zh: 衡複之榆林。

translations.literal: Heng again returned to Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was sent back to Yulin.

sentences.zh: 俄而敕衡督役江都宮。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered Heng to supervise labor on the Jiangdu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict ordered Heng to oversee construction of the Jiangdu Palace.

sentences.zh: 有人詣衡訟宮監者，衡不為理，還以訟書付監，其人大為監所困。

translations.literal: Someone went to Heng to sue the palace supervisor; Heng did not judge it and instead returned the petition to the supervisor; that man was greatly harassed by the supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Someone went to Heng to sue the palace supervisor. Heng did not judge the case and instead returned the petition to the supervisor. That man was greatly harassed by the supervisor.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書楊玄感使至江都，其人詣玄感稱冤。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan's envoy arrived at Jiangdu; that man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of rites Yang Xuangan's envoy arrived at Jiangdu. That man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.

sentences.zh: 玄感固以衡為不可。

translations.literal: Xuangan firmly considered Heng unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan was convinced that Heng was unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 及與衡相見，未有所言，又先謂玄感曰：「薛道衡真為枉死。」

translations.literal: When he met Heng and before anything was said, Heng first said to Xuangan: "Xue Daoheng was truly wrongly killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Heng, before anything was said Heng first told Xuangan, "Xue Daoheng was truly wrongly killed.

sentences.zh: 玄感具上其事，江都丞王世充又奏衡頻減頓具。

translations.literal: Xuangan fully reported the matter; Jiangdu Assistant Governor Wang Shichong also memorialized that Heng repeatedly reduced provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan fully reported the matter. Jiangdu assistant governor Wang Shichong also memorialized that Heng repeatedly reduced provisions.

sentences.zh: 帝於是發怒，鎖衡詣江都市，將斬之，久而乃釋，除名為民，放還田裡。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon flew into rage, fettered Heng to Jiangdu city, and was about to execute him; after a long time he released him, stripped him of rank and made him a commoner, and sent him back to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon flew into rage, fettered Heng in Jiangdu city, and was about to execute him. After a long time he released him, stripped him of rank, made him a commoner, and sent him back to his fields.

sentences.zh: 帝每令親人覘衡所為。

translations.literal: The Emperor often ordered close associates to observe what Heng did.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often ordered close associates to observe what Heng did.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝 自遼東還都，衡妾言衡怨望，謗訕朝政，竟賜盡於家。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Emperor returned from Liaodong to the capital; Heng's concubine said Heng harbored resentment and slandered court policy; he was ultimately granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor returned from Liaodong to the capital. Heng's concubine reported that he harbored resentment and slandered court policy. He was ultimately granted death at home.

sentences.zh: 臨死大言曰：「我為人作何物事，而望久活！」

translations.literal: Facing death he spoke loudly: "What sort of things have I done for others, yet hoped to live long!
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he cried out, "What sort of things have I done for others, yet hoped to live long!

sentences.zh: 監刑者塞耳，促令殺之。

translations.literal: The execution supervisor stopped his ears and hurried the killing.
translations.idiomatic: The execution supervisor covered his ears and urged them to carry out the sentence at once.

sentences.zh: 義寧中，以死非其罪，贈大將軍、南陽郡公，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: In Yining, because his death was not for his crime, he was posthumously granted Grand General and Duke of Nanyang Commandery, with posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: In Yining, because his death was not for his crime, he was posthumously granted grand general and duke of Nanyang commandery, with posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 有子希玄。

translations.literal: He had a son named Xixuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xixuan.

sentences.zh: ○楊汪

translations.literal: ○ Yang Wang
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wang

sentences.zh: 楊汪，字元度，本弘農華陰人也，曾祖順，徙居河東。

translations.literal: Yang Wang, styled Yuandu, was originally of Huayin in Hongnong; his great-grandfather Shun moved to settle in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wang, courtesy name Yuandu, was originally from Huayin in Hongnong. His great-grandfather Shun moved to settle in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父琛，儀同三司，及汪貴，追贈平鄉縣公。

translations.literal: His father Chen was Pillar of State, Third Rank; when Wang became honored, he was posthumously granted Duke of Pingxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen held the rank pillar of state, third rank. When Wang became honored, Chen was posthumously granted duke of Pingxiang county.

sentences.zh: 汪少凶疏，好與人群鬥，拳所毆擊，無不顛踣。

translations.literal: Wang from youth was fierce and unrestrained, fond of fighting in crowds; those struck by his fists all toppled over.
translations.idiomatic: Wang from youth was fierce and unrestrained, fond of brawling in crowds. Those struck by his fists all toppled over.

sentences.zh: 長更折節勤學，專精《左氏傳》，通《三禮》。

translations.literal: When grown he reformed himself, studied diligently, and specialized in 《Zuo Tradition》 and mastered 《Three Rites》.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he reformed himself, studied diligently, specialized in the 《Zuo Tradition》, and mastered the 《Three Rites》.

sentences.zh: 解褐周冀王侍讀，王甚重之，每曰：「楊侍讀德業優深，孤之穆生也。」

translations.literal: He began his career as Reader to Prince of Ji of Zhou; the Prince greatly valued him and often said: "Reader Yang's virtue and learning are deep and excellent—he is my Mu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as reader to Prince of Ji of Zhou. The prince greatly valued him and often said, "Reader Yang's virtue and learning are deep and excellent—he is my Mu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 其後問《禮》于沈重，受《漢書》于劉臻，二人推許之曰：「吾弗如也。」

translations.literal: Later he studied 《Rites》 under Shen Chong and received 《Book of Han》 under Liu Zhen; the two men praised him, saying: "We are not his equal."
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied the 《Rites》 under Shen Chong and received the 《Book of Han》 under Liu Zhen. The two men praised him, saying, "We are not his equal."

sentences.zh: 由是知名，累遷夏官府都上士。

translations.literal: Thereby he became renowned and was repeatedly transferred to Senior Officer of the Summer Office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he became renowned and rose to senior officer of the summer office.

sentences.zh: 及高祖居相，引知兵事，遷掌朝下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was at Xiang, he was summoned to know military affairs and transferred to Grand Master for the Court Below.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was at Xiang, he was summoned to advise on military affairs and transferred to grand master for the court below.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，賜爵平鄉縣伯，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, he was granted the rank Earl of Pingxiang County with a fief of 200 households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was granted the rank earl of Pingxiang county with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 曆尚書司勳兵部二曹侍郎、秦州總管長史，名為明幹。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Minister in the Bureaus of Merits and Military Affairs and as Chief Administrator to the Governor-General of Qin Prefecture, and was called clear and capable.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as vice minister in the bureaus of merits and military affairs and as chief administrator to the governor-general of Qin prefecture, and was called clear and competent.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，坐事免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and was dismissed on account of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left vice director of the secretariat and was dismissed on account of an affair.

sentences.zh: 後曆荊、洛二州長史，每聽政之暇，必延生徒講授，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Chief Administrator of the two prefectures of Jing and Luo; whenever he had leisure from hearing cases, he always invited students to lecture and teach, and people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he successively served as chief administrator of Jing and Luo prefectures. Whenever he had leisure from hearing cases, he always invited students to lecture and teach, and people of the day praised him.

sentences.zh: 數年，高祖謂諫議大夫王達曰：「卿為我覓一好左丞。」

translations.literal: After several years Emperor Gaozu said to Remonstrance Officer Wang Da: "Find me a good Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Emperor Gaozu said to remonstrance officer Wang Da, "Find me a good left vice director.

sentences.zh: 達遂私于汪曰：「我當薦君為左丞，若事果，當以良田相報也。」

translations.literal: Da thereupon spoke privately to Wang: "I shall recommend you as Left Vice Director; if the matter succeeds, I should repay you with good fields."
translations.idiomatic: Da thereupon spoke privately to Wang: "I shall recommend you as left vice director. If the matter succeeds, I shall repay you with good fields."

sentences.zh: 汪以達所言奏之，達竟以獲罪，卒拜汪為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Wang memorialized what Da said; Da ultimately was punished by crime and Wang was finally appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang memorialized what Da said. Da was ultimately punished for his crime, and Wang was finally appointed left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 汪明習法令，果於剖斷，當時號為稱職。

translations.literal: Wang was clearly versed in laws and statutes and decisive in judgment; at the time he was called competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was clearly versed in laws and statutes and decisive in judgment. At the time he was regarded as competent in office.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，守大理卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he served as Acting Grand Master for Law.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he served as acting grand master for law.

sentences.zh: 汪視事二日，帝將親省囚徒。

translations.literal: Wang had been in office two days when the Emperor was about to personally inspect the prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Wang had been in office two days when the emperor was about to personally inspect the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 其時系囚二百餘人，汪通宵究審，詰朝而奏，曲盡事情，一無遺誤，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: At that time bound prisoners numbered over 200; Wang examined them all night and by morning presented his report, fully covering the circumstances without a single omission or error; the Emperor greatly commended him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time over two hundred prisoners were in custody. Wang examined them all night and by morning presented his report, fully covering the circumstances without a single omission or error. The emperor greatly commended him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜國子祭酒。

translations.literal: After a little over a year he was appointed Rector of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: A year or so later he was appointed rector of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 帝令百僚就學，與汪講論，天下通儒碩學多萃焉，論難鋒起，皆不能屈。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the hundred officials to come study and debate with Wang; eminent scholars throughout the realm gathered; debate flared sharp and none could bend him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the hundred officials to come study and debate with Wang. Eminent scholars throughout the realm gathered. Debate flared sharp, and none could bend him.

sentences.zh: 帝令御史書其問答奏之，省而大悅，賜良馬一匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the censorate to write down their questions and answers and present them; he read and was greatly pleased and granted one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the censorate to write down their questions and answers and present them. He read them and was greatly pleased, granting one fine horse.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In Daye he served as Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye he served as silver-gleaming grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 及楊玄感反河南，贊治裴弘策出師禦之，戰不利，弘策出還，遇汪而屏人交語。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled in Henan, Assistant Director Pei Hongce went out with troops to resist him; the battle went badly and Hongce returned; he met Wang and dismissed others to speak with him in private.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled in Henan, assistant director Pei Hongce went out with troops to resist him. The battle went badly and Hongce returned. He met Wang and dismissed others to speak with him in private.

sentences.zh: 既而留守樊子蓋斬弘策，以狀奏汪，帝疑之，出為梁郡通守。

translations.literal: Soon Garrison Commander Fan Zigai executed Hongce and memorialized Wang's situation; the Emperor suspected him and sent him out as Administrator of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon garrison commander Fan Zigai executed Hongce and memorialized Wang's situation. The emperor suspected him and sent him out as administrator of Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 後李密已逼東都，其徒頻寇梁郡，汪勒兵拒之，頻挫其銳。

translations.literal: Later Li Mi had already pressed the Eastern Capital; his followers repeatedly raided Liang Commandery; Wang led troops to resist them and repeatedly blunted their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Mi had already pressed the eastern capital. His followers repeatedly raided Liang commandery. Wang led troops to resist them and repeatedly blunted their edge.

sentences.zh: 煬帝崩，王世充推越王侗為主，征拜吏部尚書，頗見親委。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang died, Wang Shichong installed Prince of Yue Tong as ruler and summoned Wang as Minister of Personnel; he was greatly trusted and relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang died, Wang Shichong installed Prince Tong of Yue as ruler and summoned Wang as minister of personnel. He was greatly trusted and relied upon.

sentences.zh: 及世充僭號，汪複用事，世充平，以凶黨誅死。

translations.literal: When Shichong usurped the throne, Wang again held power; when Shichong was pacified, he was executed as a villainous partisan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong usurped the throne, Wang again held power. When Shichong was pacified, Wang was executed as a villainous partisan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：盧愷諫說可稱，令狐熙所居而治，薛胄執憲平允，宇文弼聲望攸歸，張衡以鯁正立名，楊汪以學業自許。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Lu Kai's remonstrances and persuasions were commendable; Linghu Xi governed wherever he resided; Xue Zhou held the law with fairness; Yu Wenbi's reputation was universally acknowledged; Zhang Heng established his name through upright integrity; Yang Wang prided himself on scholarly achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Lu Kai's remonstrances were commendable; Linghu Xi governed wherever he resided; Xue Zhou held the law with fairness; Yu Wenbi's reputation was universally acknowledged; Zhang Heng established his name through upright integrity; Yang Wang prided himself on scholarly achievement.

sentences.zh: 然皆有善始，鮮克令終，九仞之基，俱傾於一匱，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yet all had good beginnings and few kept fine endings; foundations nine ren high all toppled in one basket—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yet all had good beginnings and few kept fine endings. Foundations nine ren high all toppled in one basket—alas!

sentences.zh: 夫忠為令德，施非其人尚或不可，況托足邪徑，而又不得其人者歟！

translations.literal: Loyalty is a fine virtue; to bestow it on the wrong person may still be impossible—how much more when one sets foot on a crooked path and yet does not obtain the right person!
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty is a fine virtue. To bestow it on the wrong person may still be impossible—how much more when one sets foot on a crooked path and yet does not obtain the right person!

sentences.zh: 語曰：「無為權首，將受其咎。」

translations.literal: The saying goes: "Do not be the head of intrigue—you will receive its calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes, "Do not be the head of intrigue—you will receive its calamity.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「無始禍，無召亂。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Do not be the beginning of calamity; do not summon disorder."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Do not be the beginning of calamity; do not summon disorder."

sentences.zh: 張衡既召亂源，實為權首，動不以順，其能不及於此乎？

translations.literal: Zhang Heng both summoned the source of disorder and was truly the head of power; his actions were not according with what is right—how could his calamity not reach this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng both summoned the source of disorder and was truly the head of power. His actions were not according with what is right—how could calamity not reach him!
